title: How T. Holder lost his band to Andy Kirk
summary: Holder drove to Dallas with the payroll, the band gave his job to Andy Kirk, and Holder started another band.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy
Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, T. Holder -- they were playing in Tulsa, Oklahoma and I understand -- I know -- see, he married a girl from my home town, from Denison, Texas, which is -- we call it the same thing. It's just a few miles different. A very beautiful lady and she had a beauty parlor in Dallas, so when they were working in Tulsa -- and I understand that T. had called home like about four or five nights and nothing, could never reach her, you know, was -- like all night long, he'd call home and she wouldn't be there. So he -- on pay night, he took the whole payroll and just jumped in his Buick and drove from Tulsa down to Dallas. So the next day, they wake up and he's gone. So they -- everybody gets nervous, all the musicians get nervous, say, 'Well, man, this cat has run off with all the money,' you know what I mean? A lot of people were doing that and the promoters were doing that in

those days. So they figured he had run off with all the money. He didn't say anything. So he didn't come back until -- he stayed a whole day. So that day, they got together and they says, "Well, we'll make Andy Kirk the leader." He was playing sousaphone in the band. So Andy told me this himself. "They gave me this man's band." So when he comes back the next evening, he called a meeting, says, "Fellas, I'm sorry," he says, "but I was having a little family trouble." He says, "But everything's all right and I got the money. I'm ready to pay you. I'm sorry I ran away with your money." And he said he never felt so badly in his life. So here they done got together and fired the man and they says, "Well, T., we didn't know. We jumped the gun too quick. We acted too quick and we've given the band to Andy Kirk." He says, "But --" They says, "But we'd like you to stay on and be a," you know, "trumpet player." So he says, "No," says, "if that's the way you feel," he says, "it's quite all right." And he left, paid them, gave them the money, left and got in his car and came back to Dallas.
Now he organized another band in two weeks that was -- topped that band. He was a builder.
